dan: Quick kickoff thread for long-term routing/isolation roadmap. Need a concise cutover checklist + launch gates that product, eng, ops, and sales can agree on. Goal: deliver Q3 slotting proposal with cost models and pilot plan.

olivia: +1. customers keep asking for predictable latency and residency. We should define 3 delivery patterns: shared (multi-tenant), committed (dedicated pools), and customer-hosted (VPC / on-prem).

priya: From research: dedicated pools give stable p95 but hurt batching. We'll need per-tenant KV namespaces and pre-warm procedures to avoid cold-start spikes.

michael: Ops: Key must-haves for launch: automated rollback, canary window, alert ownership, and documented cache rehydration steps. We also need token-level billing hooks.

zev: Product asks: sales-facing pricing bands (monthly commit tiers), expected latency deltas, and a short one-pager on migration UX (what changes for apps).

olivia: Proposed acceptance gates: performance (p95 target by lane), reliability (SLO >= 99.9% over 7d for pilot), security (KMS + audit events + role-based access), and regression-free quality (eval suite pass).

priya: Suggestion on quality gate: prod-research runs a 100-prompt eval and we require <5% degradation vs baseline for approved fallback variants. If fallback triggers, must surface examples in logs.

dan: Migration patterns: prefer staged traffic mirroring + gradual cutover (5% increments/day) rather than instant lift+shift. Mirrors allow comparing outputs and metrics before commitment.

michael: For canary: run 48h with synthetic load + 24h low-volume real traffic. Rollback if error rate > 2x or p95 regresses > 30% for 15m. Add a human ok for anything else.

zev: Sales runbook should include: expected timeline, no-downtime goal, app-level pointers (connection affinity, session stickiness), and sample billing impact. We can draft slides for executive signoff.

priya: Runtime detail: we need a traffic-splitter API supporting affinity keys (cookie / client-id) and percentage rollout. Also per-tenant KV isolation and a fast rehydration command.

olivia: Cost modeling ask: sam/team should produce 3 scenarios (low/typical/high) showing token unit cost delta and amortized GPU cost for 6/12/24 month commitments. Include burst-lane pricing if dedicated autoscaling is used.

dan: For private (on-prem): acceptance includes installer image + minimal operator docs, remote-support playbook, and signed customer SOC checklist. Launch only after compliance signoff.

michael: Telemetry: must emit p50/p95 per-tenant, KV hit ratio, cache warm percentage, token count, model-variant in use, and fallback events. SLA report exportable daily.

zev: Pricing & discounts: propose commit bands (3m/6m/12m) with progressive discounts and a guaranteed latency SLA for top band. Tie discount to observed usage band to avoid overcommit risk.

priya: Edge cases: cross-region affinity — decide whether to follow geo-routing or tenant-configured residency (customer might want EU-only). Need policy defaults and override APIs.

olivia: Migration acceptance checklist (draft):
- Pilot: 1-2 customers for 2 weeks
- Canary: synthetic 48h + real traffic 24h
- Mirroring: 5% increments/day with observability dashboards
- Quality: eval suite pass and manual sample review
- Ops: rollback playbook + owner assigned
- Billing: simulated invoice + commit tier assigned

dan: Next-step owners:
- priya: traffic-splitter API spec by Tue
- michael: canary/rollback playbook + telemetry spec by Wed
- olivia: sales one-pager + residency policy draft by Wed
- zev: pricing bands proposal by Thu
- research: eval suite & baseline run by Thu

oncall-bot: Note: roadmap doc updated at 1796661400 by dan (v1) :white_check_mark:

zev: One more: fallback policy defaults. Allow quantized/lightweight model as fallback but require explicit opt-in per-customer. Default should prefer regional model variant before cross-region.

priya: Agree. Also add a safety gate: if fallback used >5% of tokens for 24h, trigger an ops review.

michael: Ops needs a small maintenance allocation (0.2 FTE) for runbook upkeep and SLA reporting. Flagging for capacity planning.

olivia: I'll collate all items into a one-page roadmap with acceptance gates and circulate. If no objections, we lock these gates for Q3 planning sync. Please DM me any redlines. :sparkles:
